'''''Lonicera interrupta''''', commonly known as '''chaparral honeysuckle''', is a species of plant found in the western United States.

==Description==
''Lonicera interrupta'' is a shrub with a woody trunk. The leaves are up to {{Convert|3.5|cm|frac=4}} long.<ref name="tktimb">{{Cite book |last1=Turner |first1=Mark |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VLbAAwAAQBAJ |title=Trees & Shrubs of the Pacific Northwest |last2=Kuhlmann |first2=Ellen |date=2014 |publisher=[[Timber Press]] |isbn=978-1-60469-263-1 |edition=1st |location=Portland, OR |pages=307}}</ref> The plant sends up spiked [[inflorescence]]s of yellow [[honeysuckle]] flowers. Each flower is about {{Convert|1|cm|frac=4}} long,<ref name="tktimb" /> with prominent [[stamens]] extending from the rolled-back lips.

The fruits are red,<ref name="tktimb" /> spherical, and shiny.

==Distribution and habitat==
It is native to [[chaparral]] and mixed forest habitats<ref name="tktimb" /> in the foothills and mountain ranges of [[California]], and to some mountains in Arizona.

It is [[Hardiness (plants)|hardy]] and quite [[drought-tolerant]].

==Ecology==
The flowers are attractive to [[hummingbird]]s.

==Uses==
The fruits are bitter but edible, unlike many members of the genus.<ref name="tktimb" />
